text.p: Britain on Monday praised the way Albania's national election had been conducted.

"We welcome the fact that the first round of elections took place in what the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe have described as 'adequate and acceptable' conditions, and in an atmosphere of relative calm with high voter turnout," the Foreign Office said in a statement.

Albania's President Sali Berisha earlier admitted the defeat of his Democratic Party in the election. The Socialists say they expect that with allied parties, they will have a two thirds majority in the 155-seat parliament.
The election followed one 13 months ago which was found to have been unfair.

"We call on all parties to respect the democratic will of the people and to work together to overcome the challenges facing the country -- in particular the restoration of stability and the promotion of economic and political reform," the British statement said.
